stories.headline: Rhetoric and reality
stories.title: Rhetoric and reality
stories.summary: Geopolitics is rarely a single-lens issue. Chief Minister Omar Abdullah’s speech on the 80th Independence Day at Bakshi Stadium in Srinagar, reflected on some of the hard-hitting realities of the entire Jammu and Kashmir divided by Line of Control or LoC. The LoC in itself a contradiction --- an artificial, de facto border, or merely as a line on the map. Omar’s emphasis that these fault lines can only be corrected through reunification aligns with India’s core national stance. When a prominent Kashmiri leader articulates the reality, it carries a unique geopolitical weight. As the democratically elected head of J&K, he is well within his rights to address the issues concerning the territory and people across the LoC, which officially figures on the Indian map of as part of the Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir following the 2019 Reorganization. His pitch for restoring statehood and pre-August 5, 2019, constitutional guarantees has a clear backdrop. He argued that PoK residents might seek to join Jammu and Kashmir had those decisions not upended the region seven years ago. Naturally, Kashmiri politics is at play. Interpretations of the August 5 revocation—which split the erstwhile state into two Union Territories—remain divided. Yet, the promise of restoring statehood at an “appropriate time” remains central. The Centre maintains this commitment. It is waiting for the “right time”. Recent upheavals on the other side of the LoC, where Pakistani forces have unleashed all sorts of atrocities – killing people in the streets, mass arrests, clampdown on internet and media - have shattered the illusion of security in the regions named as “Azad Kashmir”. The foundations of Pakistan were laid on the basis of the religion – claiming that Hindus and Muslims were two different nations. Now that theory has gone terribly wrong. This is what Omar emphasized in his I-day speech. The people in PoK have risen against military oppression, sacrificing lives to demand freedom from the Pakistani control. And when Omar, grandson of Sheikh Mohammad Abdullah – reflects on these systemic failures, the message resonates far beyond the boundaries. We must decode his speech fairly, separating the political flair from his core stance: the return of statehood. His appeal to those across the LoC will fall flat unless he is convincing on this very issue. Ultimately, the situation presents both a complex political dilemma and an urgent demand for the restoration of statehood. The dimensions of geopolitics in South Asia have changed in recent years, particularly with regard to Jammu and Kashmir on both sides of the LoC. PoJK has been the epicentre of what Pakistan claims is the “Kashmiri struggle for the right to self-determination. “Over the decades, Pakistan has sought to limit the definition of the UN resolutions on Kashmir—envisaging a plebiscite—to this side of the Valley alone. Now, the very people of so-called “Azad Kashmir” have risen in revolt against Pakistan. The myth of a Muslim nation being the sole protector of Muslims in the region has crashed Today , the people in PoJK are sacrificing their lives to regain their freedom, which often translates into a desire to re-join Jammu and Kashmir in its totality—meaning the entire region as it existed under Maharaja Hari Singh’s rule. Technically and legally, the last Dogra king made the final decision to accede to India. However, it is significant that Kashmiris rose against Pakistani tribesmen and the army even before the Instrument of Accession (IoA) was signed. At the risk of their lives, the Muslim-majority Valley had already signalled its choice to be with India, a fact that should not be overlooked. During that crucial time, the Kashmiri leadership guided the people to declare where they stood, which served as an unequivocal declaration of accession before the formal IoA took shape. This ground reality needs to be reaffirmed, to tell Pakistan that Kashmiris had given their verdict in favour of India when it invaded the erstwhile state of Jammu and Kashmir: the people of Kashmir chose India when tribal raiders invaded the erstwhile princely state in 1947. That’s the way India can counter Pakistan and all others questioning it on Jammu and Kashmir, more effectively. This is the message that needs to be grasped and broadcast with all the authority. Who else could have reflected on this historic reality than grandson of Sheikh Abdullah who was in the frontline for leading the masses against the Pakistani invaders. This fact needs to eb appreciated . The people in PoJk, which were enslaved by Pakistani military , must have been regretting why did they miss the bus in 1947- and fell into the trap of Pakistan . History offers a telling example of how deeply the legacy worries Pakistan. In September 2001, as the world reeled from the 9/11 attacks in the US, Pakistan’s President Pervez Musharraf was visibly rattled. Why? Because Omar Abdullah, then serving as India’s Minister of State for External Affairs, had visited Dushanbe on September 13, 2001. Days later, in his September 19 address justifying Pakistan’s alliance with the US-led war on terror, Musharraf anxiously referenced that very visit to the Tajik capital. He wondered: “What was India doing in Dushanbe.”. Musharraf’s frustration stemmed from the possibility of India stepping in and snatching the geopolitical and geostrategic advantages that Pakistan had because of its location. That was his way of saying but the man who represented India and discussed the regional security in the wake of 9/11 was Omar Abdullah. The then Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee had recognized national asset in Omar Abdullah, a Kashmiri Muslim, in the international affairs. The point here is what he says about Pakistan and the affairs in the Pakistan occupied territories across the LoC, carries more weight than others saying the same thing. The Chief Minister has already spoken against the atrocities being committed on the people in PoK, and asserted and re-asserted that “the people across are our people .” This is a loud echo of what Home Minister Amit Shah has said time and again that not only the territory but also the people of PoJK are ours- whether Muslims or Hindus.
